nodes.label: Upgrade, Learning-Curve, and Dashboard Test Validation
nodes.norm_label: upgrade, learning-curve, and dashboard test validation

nodes.label: Upgrade Validation Limitations
nodes.rationale: The reported test period is an inspected historical benchmark rather than a new blind holdout; statistical significance, clean-environment reproduction, multimodal modeling, prediction intervals, and SHAP explanations were not established.

nodes.label: Linear Model Error Plateau
nodes.rationale: OLS, Ridge, and linear SVR training and validation Log RMSE change little after the smaller sample sizes, suggesting limited benefit from additional rows under the fixed engineered representation.

nodes.label: No Test Rows Used
nodes.rationale: The learning-curve experiment varies historical training size while retaining a fixed development validation period and excludes final test rows.

nodes.label: Single Seeded Learning-Curve Experiment
nodes.rationale: The plotted curves summarize one seeded experiment and therefore show model behavior for this sampling realization rather than uncertainty intervals.

nodes.label: XGBoost Validation Improvement with More Data
nodes.norm_label: xgboost validation improvement with more data
nodes.rationale: XGBoost validation Log RMSE declines steadily as the nested training sample expands, while its training error rises and the train-validation gap narrows.

nodes.norm_label: missingness audit and positional sparsity report

nodes.label: Justification Against Blanket Imputation
nodes.rationale: Feature missingness is concentrated in contract and club fields, while performance zeros vary strongly by playing position; a single imputation policy would conflate distinct data conditions.

nodes.label: Position-Dependent Structural Zero Interpretation
nodes.rationale: The large, systematic differences in zero goals and assists across positions indicate that many zeros encode role-specific outcomes rather than missing observations.

nodes.label: Football Player Market Value Trajectory vs. Age Across Positions

nodes.label: Time-Aware Valuation with Explanations and Calibrated Uncertainty
nodes.norm_label: time-aware valuation with explanations and calibrated uncertainty

nodes.label: Calendar-Fold and Fold-Local Preprocessing Repair
nodes.rationale: Row-based time folds can share dates, and preprocessing outside folds lets validation or test rows affect learned transformations; calendar blocks and fold-local fitting remove these couplings.

nodes.label: Matched-Feature Model Comparison
nodes.rationale: Ridge and XGBoost must receive the same eligible rows and inputs before performance differences can be attributed to model class.

nodes.label: Recent Form and Observation Coverage Upgrade
nodes.norm_label: recent form and observation coverage upgrade

nodes.label: Observation Coverage Modeling
nodes.rationale: Zero captured minutes can mean missing competition coverage rather than inactivity, so coverage indicators and coverage-stratified evaluation are needed.

nodes.label: Position-Prior Exposure Shrinkage
nodes.rationale: Per-90 estimates from small samples are stabilized toward training-derived position priors using 450 pseudo-minutes while retaining exposure indicators.

nodes.label: Fixed-2023 Learning Curve Protocol
nodes.rationale: Nested samples from the already historical pre-2023 pool isolate sample-size effects while a fixed 2023 validation set avoids moving the evaluation cutoff.

nodes.label: Log-Scale Distribution Stabilization
nodes.rationale: The natural-log transform reduces observed skewness from 8.55 to 0.50 and kurtosis from 114.19 to 0.18.

nodes.label: Structural Zero Preservation
nodes.rationale: Goal and assist zeros are often genuine position-specific outcomes, so blanket mean imputation would invent attacking output for defensive roles.

nodes.label: Duan Smearing Retransformation
nodes.rationale: Multiplying exponentiated predictions by an out-of-sample residual factor corrects overall mean retransformation bias, though a global factor cannot repair segment-specific bias.

nodes.label: Log Target Transformation
nodes.rationale: Logging market value reduces extreme right skew, limits superstar dominance, and makes model errors more relative across price levels.

nodes.label: Cross-Sport Generalization Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Framework reuse with separately trained sport models is not zero-shot transfer; unseen-sport claims require a held-out-sport or limited-label adaptation experiment.

nodes.label: Sport-Specific Target Semantics
nodes.rationale: Market valuation, salary, transfer fee, auction bid, and performance score are different quantities; currency conversion or normalization does not make their meanings interchangeable.

nodes.label: Chronological Validation
nodes.rationale: Random splits can place nearby valuations of the same player on both sides and expose future market levels; chronological splits better represent forecasting.

nodes.label: Missing Potential, Hype, and Brand Signal Hypothesis
nodes.norm_label: missing potential, hype, and brand signal hypothesis
nodes.rationale: The observed underprediction of young and elite-league players may reflect omitted potential, hype, or brand signals, but the report marks this explanation as untested.

nodes.label: No Good-Buy Ground Truth
nodes.rationale: The dataset has no labeled profitable-transfer or good-buy outcome, so ranking gaps are disagreements rather than validated investment recommendations.

nodes.label: Model Disagreement Rankings
nodes.rationale: Largest prediction-to-market gaps generate hypotheses about missing signals but do not identify proven bargains or errors in the reference valuation.

nodes.label: Point-in-Time Feature Engineering
nodes.rationale: Features must use only information available at each valuation date so reported performance reflects a feasible historical prediction.

nodes.label: Target Variable Distribution and Log-Transformation Assessment
nodes.norm_label: target variable distribution and log-transformation assessment

nodes.label: Cross-Sport Data Provenance and Temporal Alignment
nodes.norm_label: cross-sport data provenance and temporal alignment
nodes.rationale: Dates, identifiers, rights, label completeness, and feature cutoffs must be verified before training because mismatched sources can multiply rows or leak future performance.

nodes.label: Football Player Market-Value Prediction and Valuation Lab README
nodes.norm_label: football player market-value prediction and valuation lab readme

nodes.label: Market Value Versus Transfer Fee Distinction
nodes.norm_label: market value versus transfer fee distinction
nodes.rationale: The modeled target is a consensus estimate of market worth, whereas realized fees reflect negotiations, clauses, leverage, wages, and transaction conditions.

nodes.label: Static Historical Snapshot Caveat
nodes.rationale: The data is a fixed historical snapshot rather than a live market feed, and several physical, position, contract, and club fields reflect the later snapshot.

nodes.label: 48-Hour Extension Strategy
nodes.rationale: A short sprint should choose one substantive extension and reserve time for validation, frozen outputs, and presentation rather than attempt every possible addition.

nodes.label: Temporal Text Provenance Requirements
nodes.rationale: Scouting or news text must be independently dated before valuation, deduplicated, stripped of target-revealing clues, and evaluated on matched text-covered rows.

nodes.label: Graph-First Codebase Workflow
nodes.rationale: Query the existing knowledge graph before broad source inspection and update it after code changes so navigation stays scoped and current.

nodes.label: Project Data, Model Comparison, and Graphify Guide

nodes.label: Generated Graph Representation Limitation
nodes.rationale: Even with zero dangling endpoints, missing endpoints, self-loops, and collapsed same-endpoint edges, the graph supports navigation and discovery rather than mathematically proving that every real-world dependency was modeled.

nodes.label: Incremental Graph Count Refresh Caveat
nodes.rationale: Indexing this guide adds documentation nodes, so exact node and edge totals can change after an incremental refresh; GRAPH_REPORT.md is the authoritative source for current counts.

nodes.label: Semantic Extraction Cost Record
nodes.rationale: Semantic extraction used the active Codex session without an external Gemini API, so Graphify recorded zero external API tokens; host-agent token use was unavailable through the collaboration interface.

nodes.label: Separate Raw Tables in One DuckDB Database
nodes.norm_label: separate raw tables in one duckdb database

nodes.label: Avoid Flattening All Sources into One CSV
nodes.norm_label: avoid flattening all sources into one csv
nodes.rationale: Joining player, valuation, appearance, match, event, lineup, and transfer tables before aggregation duplicates targets, inflates statistics, creates temporal leakage risk, and copies attributes millions of times.

nodes.label: Controlled Regressor Comparison
nodes.rationale: Using the same eligible observations, target, features, fold-local preprocessing, calendar validation years, and final test period separates improvements from feature engineering from improvements due to algorithm flexibility.

nodes.label: Learning-Curve Interpretation Limit
nodes.rationale: The curves come from one seeded sampling experiment and are descriptive rather than confidence intervals or formal proof of bias and variance.

nodes.label: Linear Model Higher-Bias Interpretation
nodes.rationale: OLS, Ridge, and Linear SVR converge near 0.986 validation Log RMSE and gain little from more rows, suggesting linear functional form is a stronger limitation than training-set size.

nodes.label: LinearSVR Scalability Decision
nodes.rationale: LinearSVR demonstrates support-vector regression on 435,947 training rows, while kernel RBF SVR is avoided because it does not scale well to this sample size.

nodes.label: XGBoost Nonlinear Structure and Data Scaling
nodes.norm_label: xgboost nonlinear structure and data scaling
nodes.rationale: XGBoost validation Log RMSE improves from about 0.916 to 0.890 as training size grows because boosted trees can learn nonlinear relationships and interactions among age, position, competition, exposure, and recent performance.
